newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares put on more gains, eye 1,200 pts.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares put on more gains, eye 1,200 pts.

text.p: Greek stocks headed higher on Thursday with the benchmark index climbing 1.26 percent on heavy volume as construction and industrials led the advance.
Market watchers said the next test would be at the 1,200 points resistance level.

"We had a strong market with a shift of interest into mid-cap stocks. Construction and industrials led the climb. The market will soon test the significant resistance level of 1,200 points," said Interbank relationship manager Costas Noitakis.
If the index pierces the 1,200 level on strong volume it will cruise higher but this is considered a significant resistance level, he said.

Meanwhile, defiant farmers, playing a cat-and-mouse game with police on Greek highways, asked for a meeting with Prime Minister Costas Simitis on Thursday and vowed not to block roads for 24 hours in a show of goodwill.

Simitis has so far turned down requests by farmers to meet, saying flatly that the government won't bow to threats of a new blockade and that it can't satisfy their demands for cheaper fuel and state subsidies.
The Athens general share index finished 1.26 percent or 14.88 points higher at 1194.72 points from Wednesday's 1179.84, after opening at 1176.71.
Gainers led losers 129 to 76 with 36 issues unchanged on 241 traded. Turnover was 16.5 billion drachmas on volume of 6.04 million shares.
Banks firmed 0.48 percent, construction shares jumped 2.20 percent along with industrials, up 2.67 percent. Small-caps ended 0.45 percent higher.
